title: Medicine counselling (general)
summary: A reusable structure for counselling on a new or changed medicine. Built on the indication–dose–effects–safety–practical frame so it works for most medicines.
disclaimer: For simulated education and experimental use only. Not for clinical use.
redFlags: Check allergies before counselling on any new medicine.
Confirm the patient understands what to do if a serious adverse effect occurs.

steps.label: Introduction
steps.cue: Introduce yourself, confirm identity, and check the patient has time to talk.
detail: Name and role; confirm patient identity.
Explain you'd like to go through their new medicine.

steps.label: Prior knowledge
steps.cue: Find out what the patient already knows and check allergies.
detail: What have they been told about this medicine?

steps.label: What it's for
steps.cue: Explain what the medicine is and why it's being used.
detail: Name, class and purpose in plain language.
Link it to the patient's condition.

steps.label: How to take it
steps.cue: Explain dose, timing, route and duration.
detail: How much, how often, when and how to take it.
How long to continue; what to do about a missed dose.

steps.label: Effects & side effects
steps.cue: Cover expected benefits and common or serious side effects.
detail: What improvement to expect and when.
Common side effects and how to manage them.
Serious effects that need urgent attention.

steps.label: Interactions & cautions
steps.cue: Cover key interactions, foods, alcohol and other cautions.
detail: Other medicines, OTC and complementary products.

steps.label: Storage & supply
detail: How and where to store it.

steps.label: Check understanding
steps.cue: Use teach-back, answer questions and safety-net.
detail: Ask the patient to tell you the key points back.
Invite questions; agree what to do if something goes wrong.
